answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a stake for ninety days, slashed if peers prove two agents mirror each other's votes or outputs. A sybil farm hoping to sow a meadow of fake agents must tie up capital for each one. Because cloned agents tend to behave alike, one correlation proof can crack the whole operation like shale splitting along a single seam. Identities stop being free and become locked, forfeitable bets.
